neet_che_u17_t00_1.working: Lucas reagent reacts by an SN1 path through a carbocation. A tertiary alcohol such as 2-methylpropan-2-ol forms the most stable carbocation, so it gives turbidity immediately. Secondary alcohols react within about 5 minutes, and primary alcohols do not react at room temperature.

neet_che_u17_t00_2.working: Heated Cu at 573 K dehydrogenates secondary alcohols to ketones. Butan-2-ol is the only secondary alcohol among the options, and it gives butanone.

neet_che_u17_t00_3.working: Immediate turbidity means X is tertiary, so X is 2-methylpropan-2-ol. A tertiary alcohol has no α-H for dehydrogenation, so over Cu at 573 K it undergoes dehydration instead and gives 2-methylpropene.

neet_che_u17_t00_4.working: A is true. R is also true and explains A: the stable 3° carbocation leads to fast chloride formation, and the chloride is insoluble, which causes the turbidity.

neet_che_u17_t00_5.working: Statement I is correct because PCC stops the oxidation at the aldehyde. Statement II is wrong because a tertiary alcohol has no H on the carbinol carbon and so resists mild oxidation.
